18649-some-diversions-of-a-man-of-letter.creator: Edmund Gosse, C.B.
18649-some-diversions-of-a-man-of-letter.description: A book by Edmund Gosse, C.B.. etry, he dedicated his first chapter to "Differences of Taste in Nations." A critic of to-day might well find it necessary, on the threshold of a general inquiry, to expatiate on "Differences of Taste in Generations." Changes of standard in the arts are always taking place, but it is only with advancing years, perhaps, that we begin to be embarrassed by the recurrence of them.

55298-her-husband-s-purse.creator: Helen R. Martin
55298-her-husband-s-purse.description: A book by Helen R. Martin. "To think he'd leave us learn about it in the newspapers yet, sooner 'n he'd come home and face us with it! Yes, it looks anyhow as if he was ashamed of the girl he's picked out!" exclaimed Jennie, a stern and uncompromising spinster of sixty, as she and her sister Sadie, sitting in the elaborately furnished and quite hideous sitting-room of their big, fine house on Main Street, stared in consternation at the glaring headlines of the New Munich _Evening Intelligencer_, which announced,

arxiv-2112-00852.title: Unbound Close Stellar Encounters in the Solar Neighborhood
arxiv-2112-00852.creator: Bradley M. S. Hansen
arxiv-2112-00852.description: Abstract We present a catalog of unbound stellar pairs, within 100 pc of the Sun, that are undergoing close, hyperbolic, encounters. The data are drawn from the GAIA EDR3 catalogue, and the limiting factors are errors in the radial distance and unknown velocities along the line of sight.

arxiv-2301-06845.title: Causal Models with Constraints
arxiv-2301-06845.creator: Sander Beckers, Joseph Y. Halpern, Christopher Hitchcock
arxiv-2301-06845.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sander Beckers, Joseph Y. Halpern, Christopher Hitchcock. Causal models have proven extremely useful in offering formal representations of causal relationships between a set of variables. Yet in many situations, there are non-causal relationships among variables.

arxiv-2309-03561.title: Trinary Decision Trees for handling missing data
arxiv-2309-03561.creator: Henning Zakrisson Department of Mathematics, Stockholm University
arxiv-2309-03561.description: Abstract . This paper introduces the Trinary decision tree, an algorithm designed to improve the handling of missing data in decision tree regressors and classifiers. Unlike other approaches, the Trinary decision tree does not assume that missing values contain any information about the response.

arxiv-2312-06117.title: M3SOT: Multi-frame, Multi-field, Multi-space 3D Single Object Tracking
arxiv-2312-06117.creator: Jiaming Liu, Yue Wu, Maoguo Gong, Qiguang Miao, Wenping Ma, Can Qin
arxiv-2312-06117.description: Abstract 3D Single Object Tracking (SOT) stands a forefront task of computer vision, proving essential for applications like autonomous driving. Sparse and occluded data in scene point clouds introduce variations in the appearance of tracked objects, adding complexity to the task.

arxiv-2411-02562.title: Segment Anything for Dendrites from Electron Microscopy Thanks: * Corresponding Authors
arxiv-2411-02562.creator: 1 st Zewen Zhuo * A.I. Virtanen Institute for Molecular Sciences University of Eastern Finland Kuopio, Finland zewen.zhuo@uef.fi 2 nd Ilya Belevich Electron Microscopy Unit Institute of Biotechnology University of Helsinki Helsinki, Finland ilya.belevich@helsinki.fi 3 rd Ville Leinonen Department of
arxiv-2411-02562.description: Abstract Segmentation of cellular structures in electron microscopy (EM) images is fundamental to analyzing the morphology of neurons and glial cells in the healthy and diseased brain tissue. Current neuronal segmentation applications are based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and do not effectively capture global relationships within images.

arxiv-2506-03133.title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
arxiv-2506-03133.creator: Kai Lion Liang Zhang Bingcong Li Niao He *
arxiv-2506-03133.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kai Lion Liang Zhang Bingcong Li Niao He *. We show that low-rank adaptation of large-scale models suffers from a low stable rank that is well below the linear algebraic rank of the subspace, degrading fine-tuning performance. To mitigate the underutilization of the allocated subspace, we propose PoLAR, a parameterization inspired by the polar decomposition that factorizes the low-rank update into two direction matrices constrained to Stiefel manifolds and an unconstrained scale matrix.

arxiv-2509-03394.title: CloudFormer: An Attention-based Performance Prediction for Public Clouds with Unknown Workload
arxiv-2509-03394.creator: Amirhossein Shahbazinia, Darong Huang, Luis Costero, David Atienza
arxiv-2509-03394.description: Abstract Cloud platforms are increasingly relied upon to host diverse, resource-intensive workloads due to their scalability, flexibility, and cost-efficiency. In multi-tenant cloud environments, virtual machines are consolidated on shared physical servers to improve resource utilization. While virtualization guarantees resource partitioning for CPU, memory, and storage, it cannot ensure performance isolation.

arxiv-2510-23347.title: Macroeconomic Forecasting for the G7 countries under Uncertainty Shocks
arxiv-2510-23347.creator: Shovon Sengupta 1,2,3 , Sunny Kumar Singh 2 , Tanujit Chakraborty 1,4 1 SAFIR, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. 2 BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, India. 3 Fidelity Investments, Boston, USA. 4 Sorbonne Center for Artificial Intelligence, Sorbonne University, Paris, France
arxiv-2510-23347.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shovon Sengupta 1,2,3 , Sunny Kumar Singh 2 , Tanujit Chakraborty 1,4 1 SAFIR, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. 2 BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, India. 3 Fidelity Investments, Boston, USA. 4 Sorbonne Center for Artificial Intelligence, Sorbonne University, Paris, France. Accurate macroeconomic forecasting has become harder amid geopolitical disruptions, policy reversals, and volatile financial markets. Conventional vector autoregressions (VARs) overfit in high-dimensional settings, while threshold VARs struggle with time-varying interdependencies and complex parameter structures.

arxiv-2601-10094.title: V-Zero: Self-Improving Multimodal Reasoning with Zero Annotation
arxiv-2601-10094.creator: Han Wang, Yi Yang, Jingyuan Hu, Minfeng Zhu, Wei Chen
arxiv-2601-10094.description: Abstract Recent advances in multimodal learning have significantly enhanced the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs). However, state-of-the-art approaches rely heavily on large-scale human-annotated datasets, which are costly and time-consuming to acquire. To overcome this limitation, we introduce V-Zero , a general post-training framework that facilitates self-improvement using exclusively unlabeled images.

arxiv-2602-16932.title: RankEvolve: Automating the Discovery of Retrieval Algorithms via LLM-Driven Evolution CCS: Information systems Retrieval models and ranking
arxiv-2602-16932.creator: Jinming Nian, Fangchen Li, Dae Hoon Park, Yi Fang
arxiv-2602-16932.description: Abstract . Retrieval algorithms like BM25 and query likelihood with Dirichlet smoothing remain strong and efficient first-stage rankers, yet improvements have mostly relied on parameter tuning and human intuition. We investigate whether a large language model, guided by an evaluator and evolutionary search, can automatically discover improved lexical retrieval algorithms.

arxiv-2602-21170.title: cyclinbayes : Bayesian Causal Discovery with Linear Non-Gaussian Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphical Models
arxiv-2602-21170.creator: Robert D. Lee robderdylee@stat.tamu.edu, Raymond K. W. Wong raywong@tamu.edu, Yang Ni yang.ni@austin.utexas.edu
arxiv-2602-21170.description: Abstract We introduce cyclinbayes , an open-source R package for discovering linear causal relationships with both acyclic and cyclic structures. The package employs scalable Bayesian approaches with spike-and-slab priors to learn directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and directed cyclic graphs (DCGs) under non-Gaussian noise.

pmc-11355322.title: Examination of Vitreolenticular Interface in Relation to Different Phacoemulsification Parameters in Early and Late Postoperative Period
pmc-11355322.creator: Ágnes Elekes, Péter Vámosi
pmc-11355322.description: Background: The surgical parameters of phacoemulsification can significantly impact the behavior of the anterior hyaloid membrane (AHM). Methods: In this prospective study, anterior segment optical coherence tomography was used to examine the attachment or detachment of the AHM of 82 eyes after uneventful phacoemulsification preoperatively and postoperatively over 1 year.

pmc-11402327.title: Establishing network pharmacology between natural polyphenols and Alzheimer’s disease using bioinformatic tools – An advancement in Alzheimer’s research
pmc-11402327.creator: Arunkumar Subramanian, T Tamilanban, Vetriselvan Subramaniyan, Mahendran Sekar, Vipin Kumar, Ashok Kumar Janakiraman, Saminathan Kayarohanam
pmc-11402327.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a major cause of disability and one of the top causes of mortality globally. AD remains a major public health challenge due to its prevalence, impact on patients and caregivers, and the current lack of a cure. In recent years, polyphenols have garnered attention for their potential therapeutic effects on AD.

pmc-11431466.title: Analytical Validation of Esopredict, an Epigenetic Prognostic Assay for Patients with Barrett’s Esophagus
pmc-11431466.creator: Sarah Laun, Francia Pierre, Suji Kim, Daniel Lunz, Tara Maddala, Jerome V Braun, Stephen J Meltzer, Lisa Kann, Robert D Odze
pmc-11431466.description: EsopredictTM is a prognostic assay that risk-stratifies Barrett’s esophagus patients to predict future progression to high-grade dysplasia (HGD) or esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Established based on foundational studies at Johns Hopkins University, a risk algorithm was developed and clinically validated in two independent studies (n = 320).

pmc-11463968.title: Preclinical evaluation of targeted therapies for central nervous system metastases
pmc-11463968.creator: Alexander J. Pfeil, Joshua D. Hale, Tiger S. Zhang, Kentaro Wakayama, Isao Miyazaki, Igor Odintsov, Romel Somwar
pmc-11463968.description: The central nervous system (CNS) represents a site of sanctuary for many metastatic tumors when systemic therapies that control the primary tumor cannot effectively penetrate intracranial lesions. Non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLCs) are the most likely of all neoplasms to metastasize to the brain, with up to 60% of patients developing CNS metastases during the disease process.

pmc-11671271.title: Unveiling the molecular landscape of PCOS: identifying hub genes and causal relationships through bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization
pmc-11671271.creator: Yifang He, Yanli Wang, Xiali Wang, Shuangping Deng, Dandan Wang, Qingqing Huang, Guorong Lyu
pmc-11671271.description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine disorder with various contributing factors. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying PCOS is essential for developing effective treatments. This study aimed to identify hub genes and investigate potential molecular mechanisms associated with PCOS through a combination of bioinformatics analysis and Mendelian randomization (MR).

pmc-12094082.title: Breaking Barriers: The Design and Development of an Assistive Technology Web App for Older Latinos with Disabilities in Daily Activities
pmc-12094082.creator: Elsa M Orellano-Colón, Adriana I Ramos-Marichal, Valeria R González-Crespo, Bianca N Zeballos-Hernández, Kenneth N Ruiz-Márquez, Abiel Roche-Lima, Joan M Adorno-Mercado, Norman A Laborde-Torres, Joshua G Berríos-Llopart, Angely M Cruz-Ramos, Dana V Montenegro, Carmen E Lamoutte, Natasha D Rosa-Casil
pmc-12094082.description: Latinos are among the populations who are the least likely to use assistive technology (AT) despite being a population with a high prevalence of functional disabilities (FDs). We aimed to create and test the usability of an AT web app for independent-living older adults with FDs.

pmc-12377321.title: Sex- and Age-based Comparison of Key Clinical Markers of Immunity After Heart and Kidney Transplantation
pmc-12377321.creator: Whitney A. Perry, Jennifer K. Chow, Audrey E. Martino, Nicholas E. Heger, Aleah Holmes, Alexandra Werner, Marta Rodriguez Garcia, Amanda R. Vest, Ashtar Chami, Pritha Sen, David R. Snydman
pmc-12377321.description: Background.The combined effects of age and sex impact important posttransplant outcomes. Despite key physiologic differences in metabolic and immune function, older women are often indiscriminately grouped with either young women or older men. We examined sex- and age-based differences in clinical markers of immunity in heart and kidney recipients, with specific attention to those of postmenopausal women.Methods.

pmc-12505076.title: Toxic microbiome and progression of chronic kidney disease: insights from a longitudinal CKD-Microbiome Study
pmc-12505076.creator: Manolo Laiola, Laetitia Koppe, Amine Larabi, Florence Thirion, Céline Lange, Benoit Quinquis, Aymeric David, Emmanuelle Le Chatelier, Berengere Benoit, Giuseppina Sequino, Stephanie Chanon, Aurelie Vieille-Marchiset, Yves-Edouard Herpe, Jean-Claude Alvarez, Griet Glorieux, Hubert Krukowski, Geert RB

pmc-12560529.title: Refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias following entrectinib initiation in metastatic lung adenocarcinoma: a case report
pmc-12560529.creator: Lili Tang, Weiwei Wan, Hongtao Zhang, Xiaoyue Li
pmc-12560529.description: BackgroundEntrectinib is a targeted therapy that has been approved for the treatment of ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer. However, this therapy is associated with known but rare cardiotoxic risks.Case presentationWe report a case of ventricular tachyarrhythmias occurring on day 4 after entrectinib initiation in a 37-year-old Han Chinese man with ROS1-positive metastatic lung adenocarcinoma.

pmc-12645680.title: Efficacy and safety of probiotic supplements on cognitive function: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
pmc-12645680.creator: Nancy Calzada-Gonzales, Ismael Moreno-Colina, Linn Chu-Fuentes, Daniel Andrade-Girón, Hugo E Tito-Chura, Carlos Quispe-Vicuña, Pedro I Torres-Balarezo, Anthony Bautista-Pariona, Joshuan J Barboza
pmc-12645680.description: ObjectiveThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of probiotic supplementation on cognitive function in individuals over 18 years of age.MethodsRandomized clinical trials (RCTs) assessing the impact of probiotics on cognitive function were included. Searches were conducted across four medical databases from inception to August 2024.

pmc-13145969.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1131 A BIOMARKER COMING OF AGE: SKIN AUTOFLUORESCENCE PREDICTS FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME AFTER ANEURYSMAL SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE
pmc-13145969.creator: Alexandra Filipov, Martin Andermann, Silvia Schönenberger, Markus Moehlenbruch, Peter Arthur Ringleb, Jessica Jesser, Christoph Gumbinger
pmc-13145969.description: Background and aimsRisk stratification after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) remains challenging. Beyond hemorrhage severity, chronic metabolic vulnerability may contribute to secondary brain injury. Skin autofluorescence (SAF) is a non-invasive bedside biomarker reflecting tissue accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). Its prognostic relevance after aSAH is undertermined.

pmc-13668165.title: Increased incidence of glaucoma and intraocular pressure fluctuation after vitrectomy for macular hole and macular pucker
pmc-13668165.creator: Tsung-En Huang, Eugene Yu-Chuan Kang, Chu-Yen Huang, Henry Shen-Lih Chen, Yu-Ching Wang, Wei-Chi Wu, Yung-Sung Lee
pmc-13668165.description: PURPOSE:To investigate the incidence of glaucoma and changes in intraocular pressure fluctuation (IOPF) after vitrectomy for macular pucker (MP) and macular hole (MH).MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 778 patients who underwent only one vitrectomy for MP or MH were enrolled from the Chang Gung Research Database.
